questions.question: Given a function [latex]f(x,y) = 4x^{2}+6y^{2}- 8x - 4y + 8. [/latex] The optimal value of f(x,y)
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} f\left ( x, y \right )&=4x^{2}+6y^{2}-8x-4y+8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=8x-8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}&=12y-4y \\ \text{Putting, } \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=0 \\ \text{and } \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} =0 \\ 8x-8&=0 \\ \text{and }12y-4y&=0\\ \text{Given, } x&=1 \text{ and }y=\frac{1}{3} \\ \left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )& \text{ is the only stationary point.}\\  r&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=8 \\   s&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial xdy} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=0 \\   t&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=12 \\ \text{Since, } rt&=8\times 12=48 \\  s^{2}&=0\\ \text{Since, }rt \gt s^{2},\end{aligned}[/latex] we have either a maxima or minima at [latex]\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )[/latex] also since, [latex]r=\left [ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{1,\, \frac{1}{3}}=8 \gt 0[/latex], the point [latex]\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )[/latex] is a point of minima. The minimum value is, [latex]f\left ( 1,\frac{1}{3} \right )=4\times 1^{2}+6\times \frac{1}{3^{2}-8\times 1-4\times \frac{1}{3}+8} =\frac{10}{3}[/latex] So the optimal value of f(x, y) is a minimum equal to [latex]\frac{10}{3}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} f\left ( x, y \right )&=4x^{2}+6y^{2}-8x-4y+8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=8x-8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}&=12y-4y \\ \text{Putting, } \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=0 \\ \text{and } \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} =0 \\ 8x-8&=0 \\ \text{and }12y-4y&=0\\ \text{Given, } x&=1 \text{ and }y=\frac{1}{3} \\ \left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )& \text{ is the only stationary point.}\\ r&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=8 \\ s&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial xdy} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=0 \\ t&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=12 \\ \text{Since, } rt&=8\times 12=48 \\ s^{2}&=0\\ \text{Since, }rt \gt s^{2},\end{aligned}[/latex]
we have either a maxima or minima at [latex]\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )[/latex]
also since, [latex]r=\left [ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{1,\, \frac{1}{3}}=8 \gt 0[/latex], the point [latex]\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )[/latex] is a point of minima.
The minimum value is,
[latex]f\left ( 1,\frac{1}{3} \right )=4\times 1^{2}+6\times \frac{1}{3^{2}-8\times 1-4\times \frac{1}{3}+8} =\frac{10}{3}[/latex]
So the optimal value of f(x, y) is a minimum equal to [latex]\frac{10}{3}[/latex]

questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} f\left ( x, y \right )&=4x^{2}+6y^{2}-8x-4y+8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=8x-8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}&=12y-4y \\ \text{Putting, } \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=0 \\ \text{and } \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} =0 \\ 8x-8&=0 \\ \text{and }12y-4y&=0\\ \text{Given, } x&=1 \text{ and }y=\frac{1}{3} \\ \left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )& \text{ is the only stationary point.}\\  r&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=8 \\   s&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial xdy} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=0 \\   t&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=12 \\ \text{Since, } rt&=8\times 12=48 \\  s^{2}&=0\\ \text{Since, }rt \gt s^{2},\end{aligned}[/latex] we have either a maxima or minima at [latex]\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )[/latex] also since, [latex]r=\left [ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{1,\, \frac{1}{3}}=8 \gt 0[/latex], the point [latex]\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )[/latex] is a point of minima. The minimum value is, [latex]f\left ( 1,\frac{1}{3} \right )=4\times 1^{2}+6\times \frac{1}{3^{2}-8\times 1-4\times \frac{1}{3}+8} =\frac{10}{3}[/latex] So the optimal value of f(x, y) is a minimum equal to [latex]\frac{10}{3}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} f\left ( x, y \right )&=4x^{2}+6y^{2}-8x-4y+8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=8x-8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}&=12y-4y \\ \text{Putting, } \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=0 \\ \text{and } \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} =0 \\ 8x-8&=0 \\ \text{and }12y-4y&=0\\ \text{Given, } x&=1 \text{ and }y=\frac{1}{3} \\ \left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )& \text{ is the only stationary point.}\\ r&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=8 \\ s&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial xdy} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=0 \\ t&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=12 \\ \text{Since, } rt&=8\times 12=48 \\ s^{2}&=0\\ \text{Since, }rt \gt s^{2},\end{aligned}[/latex]
we have either a maxima or minima at [latex]\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )[/latex]
also since, [latex]r=\left [ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{1,\, \frac{1}{3}}=8 \gt 0[/latex], the point [latex]\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )[/latex] is a point of minima.
The minimum value is,
[latex]f\left ( 1,\frac{1}{3} \right )=4\times 1^{2}+6\times \frac{1}{3^{2}-8\times 1-4\times \frac{1}{3}+8} =\frac{10}{3}[/latex]

When fast moving vehicle travels along a summit 
curve the centrifugal force will act upwards 
against gravity and hence a part of the pressure 
on the tyres and spring of the vehicle suspensions 
is relieved. So there is no problem of discomfort 
to passengers on Summit curves. The only 
problem is designing summit curves is to provide 
adequate sight distances. Circular summit curve is ideal curve as the sight 
distance available throughout the length of circular >
curve is constant. The deviation angles in vertical 
curves of highways are very small and so between 
the same tangent points, a simple parabola is 
nearly congruent with a circular arc; also a 
parabola is very easy for arithmetical manipulation 
for computing ordinates. Thus, in actual practice 
a simple parabolic curve is used as a summit 
curve instead of the circular arc.
